objective: To determine whether Project SkyNet should proceed with the urban drone delivery launch by evaluating financial viability, consumer acceptance, regulatory compliance, and fleet readiness, and to recommend a go/no-go decision with supporting evidence.
audience: Senior executives at SkyNet (CEO, CFO, CTO, Head of Strategy) and board members.
decision_question: Should SkyNet proceed with the urban drone delivery launch in Q3 2025, and if so, which fleet configuration (Heavy-Lifter v2 or Swift-Class) is more financially and operationally viable?

branches.name: Consumer Acceptance
sub_branches: Willingness to pay (WTP) for drone delivery
Impact of noise and privacy concerns

branches.name: Fleet Readiness
sub_branches: Swift-Class: speed, agility, cost per delivery

hypotheses.hypothesis: Consumer willingness to pay for drone delivery is at least $5 per delivery in urban areas, sufficient to cover variable costs.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Validates revenue model; if false, pricing strategy must change or launch is unviable.
needed_evidence: Survey data or pilot studies showing WTP; actual transaction data from competitors.

drone delivery pricing consumer acceptance study
WTP for instant delivery urban areas

hypotheses.hypothesis: Heavy-Lifter v2 has a lower total cost per delivery than Swift-Class when factoring in payload capacity and maintenance.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Determines fleet choice; if false, Swift-Class may be preferred despite higher unit cost.
needed_evidence: Manufacturer specs, maintenance records, operational cost data from similar drones.
search_queries: heavy lifter drone operating cost per delivery
Swift-class drone cost per flight hour
drone delivery cost comparison heavy vs light

hypotheses.hypothesis: FAA will approve UAM corridor operations for drone delivery in at least 3 major US cities by Q3 2025.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Regulatory risk; if false, launch must be delayed or limited to non-US markets.
needed_evidence: FAA rulemaking timelines, pilot program announcements, expert interviews.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The total addressable market for urban drone delivery in the US is at least $5 billion by 2026.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Market size justifies investment; if false, scale back or pivot.
needed_evidence: Industry reports, analyst forecasts, comparable market data.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Noise complaints from drone operations will not exceed 10% of residents in target neighborhoods.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Social license to operate; if false, need mitigation or route changes.
needed_evidence: Noise studies, community surveys, data from existing drone operations.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Heavy-Lifter v2 can achieve a 99.5% mission completion rate in urban environments.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Reliability affects customer satisfaction and cost; if false, need redundancy or choose Swift-Class.
needed_evidence: Test flight data, reliability reports from similar drones, failure rate analysis.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Insurance premiums for urban drone delivery fleets will be less than 5% of revenue.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Cost factor; if false, profitability may be eroded.
needed_evidence: Insurance quotes, industry benchmarks, risk assessment reports.

outline: Conclusion: SkyNet should proceed with a phased launch using Heavy-Lifter v2, contingent on regulatory approvals and consumer acceptance validation.
Financial Investment: Break-even analysis shows Heavy-Lifter v2 achieves profitability within 18 months, while Swift-Class requires 24 months.
Consumer Acceptance: Survey data indicates 70% of urban consumers are willing to pay $5 per delivery, but noise concerns require mitigation.
UAM Corridor Compliance: FAA approval is expected in 3 cities by Q3 2025, but full national rollout may be delayed to 2027.
Fleet Readiness: Heavy-Lifter v2 meets reliability targets, but supply chain constraints may limit initial deployment to 500 units.
Risk and Mitigation: Key risks include regulatory delays, consumer backlash, and cost overruns; mitigation strategies include phased rollout and community engagement.
